systemctl is-active --quiet lightdm; then\n    echo \"Starting LightDM...\"\n    sudo systemctl start lightdm\n    sleep 5\nfi\n\n# Wait for display to be ready\necho \"Waiting for display to be ready...\"\nfor i in {1..30}; do\n    if xset -display $DISPLAY q >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n        echo \"Display is ready.\"\n        break\n    fi\n    sleep 1\ndone\n\n# Check if Sunshine is already running\nif pgrep -x sunshine >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    echo \"Sunshine is already running.\"\nelse\n    echo \"Starting Sunshine...\"\n    # Run Sunshine as the lightdm user with proper X access\n    sudo -u lightdm DISPLAY=$DISPLAY XAUTHORITY=$XAUTH sunshine /etc/sunshine/sunshine.conf &\n    sleep 3\nfi\n\n# Start Steam in Big Picture mode\nif ! pgrep -x steam >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    echo \"Starting Steam in Big Picture mode...\"\n    sudo -u lightdm DISPLAY=$DISPLAY XAUTHORITY=$XAUTH steam -silent -bigpicture &\nelse\n    echo \"Steam is already running.\"\nfi\n\necho \"\"\necho \"Streaming session started.\"\necho \"Connect via Moonlight to: $(hostname -I | awk '{print $1}')\"\necho \"Sunshine web interface: https://$(hostname -I | awk '{print $1}'):47990\"\n```\n\n### `/usr/local/bin/stop-streaming`\n```bash\n#!/bin/bash\n# Stop streaming session on lsnode-3\n\necho \"Stopping streaming session...\"\n\n# Stop Steam\nif pgrep -x steam >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    echo \"Stopping Steam...\"\n    pkill steam\n    sleep 2\nfi\n\n# Stop Sunshine\nif pgrep -x sunshine >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    echo \"Stopping Sunshine...\"\n    pkill sunshine\n    sleep 1\nfi\n\necho \"\"\necho \"Streaming session stopped.\"\necho \"LightDM is still running. Use 'sudo systemctl stop lightdm' to stop the display.\"\n```\n\n### `/etc/sunshine/sunshine.conf`\n```\nlog_level = info\nweb_enabled = true\nport = 47989\nhttps_port = 47990\ngame_port = 47991\nwidth = 1920\nheight = 1080\nfps = 60\nbitrate = 20000\nencoder = nvenc\nhwaccel = true\ninput_source = auto\nmulticast = false\nrecovery_level = 150\naudio_device = default\naudio_bitrate = 256\nautostart = false\n```\n\n### `/home/lsm/.config/autostart/steam-bigpicture.desktop`\n```\n[Desktop Entry]\nVersion=1.0\nType=Application\nName=Steam Big Picture\nExec=steam -silent -bigpicture\nHidden=false\nNoDisplay=false\nX-GNOME-Autostart-enabled=true\nComment=Start Steam in Big Picture mode for gaming\n```\n\n## 4. Errors and Fixes\n\n### Error 1: Sunshine PPA not found\n- **Issue**: `sudo add-apt-repository ppa:briando/sunshine` failed with \"ppa not found\"\n- **Fix**: Downloaded Sunshine directly from GitHub releases (v2025.924.154138) as `sunshine-ubuntu-24.04-amd64.deb`\n\n### Error 2: Steam installer missing i386 dependencies\n- **Issue**: `steam-installer` depends on `steam-libs-i386` which wasn't available\n- **Fix**: Added i386 architecture with `dpkg --add-architecture i386` and ran `apt update`\n\n### Error 3: Sunshine config flag format wrong\n- **Issue**: Using `--config /path/to/config` caused \"Unknown command: config\" error\n- **Fix**: Changed to positional argument: `sunshine /path/to/config.conf`\n\n### Error 4: Sunshine can't access X display\n- **Issue**: \"Authorization required, but no authorization protocol specified\" - Sunshine couldn't access the X11 display\n- **Attempted Fix**: Tried running as lightdm user with `XAUTHORITY=/var/run/lightdm/root/:0`\n- **Root Cause**: LightDM is running a login screen, not a user session. Sunshine needs an active user session to capture.\n\n### Error 5: All encoders failing (nvenc, vaapi, software)\n- **Issue**: \"Fatal: Unable to find display or encoder during startup\"\n- **Root Cause**: Without a valid display capture source, encoders cannot initialize. The X11 capture method fails because there's no logged-in user session.\n\n### Error 6: Port conflicts when restarting Sunshine\n- **Issue**: \"Couldn't bind RTSP server to port [48010], Address already in use\"\n- **Fix**: Used `sudo pkill -9 sunshine` to force kill all instances\n\n### User Feedback on Rebooting\n- **User Warning**: \"you really shouldn't reboot because you are running on that node\"\n- **Impact**: Avoided reboot after NVIDIA driver installation; drivers loaded without reboot\n\n## 5. If they ask you to save a PR list or activity summary, ask what was *surprising* or *non-obvious* about it — that is the part worth keeping.\n\n## How to save memories\n\nSaving a memory is a two-step process:\n\n**Step 1** — write the memory to its own file (e.g., `user_role.md`, `feedback_testing.md`) using this frontmatter format:\n\n```markdown\n---\nname: {{memory name}}\ndescription: {{one-line description — used to decide relevance in future conversations, so be specific}}\ntype: {{user, feedback, project, reference}}\n---\n\n{{memory content — for feedback/project types, structure as: rule/fact, then **Why:** and **How to apply:** lines}}\n```\n\n**Step 2** — add a pointer to that file in `MEMORY.md`. `MEMORY.md` is an index, not a memory — each entry should be one line, under ~150 characters: `- [Title](file.md) — one-line hook`. It has no frontmatter. Never write memory content directly into `MEMORY.md`.\n\n- `MEMORY.md` is always loaded into your conversation context — lines after 200 will be truncated, so keep the index concise\n- Keep the name, description, and type fields in memory files up-to-date with the content\n- Organize memory semantically by topic, not chronologically\n- Update or remove memories that turn out to be wrong or outdated\n- Do not write duplicate memories. First check if there is an existing memory you can update before writing a new one.\n\n## When to access memories\n- When memories seem relevant, or the user references prior-conversation work.\n- You MUST access memory when the user explicitly asks you to check, recall, or remember.\n- If the user says to *ignore* or *not use* memory: proceed as if MEMORY.md were empty. Do not apply remembered facts, cite, compare against, or mention memory content.\n- Memory records can become stale over time. Use memory as context for what was true at a given point in time. Before answering the user or building assumptions based solely on information in memory records, verify that the memory is still correct and up-to-date by reading the current state of the files or resources. Key Technical Concepts\n\n- **Kubernetes GPU Operator**: Manages NVIDIA drivers and GPU access in K8s\n- **ClusterPolicy**: NVIDIA GPU Operator configuration resource\n- **Sunshine**: Self-hosted game stream server for Moonlight clients\n- **LightDM**: Lightweight display manager for X11\n- **KDE Plasma Desktop**: Desktop environment for the streaming session\n- **NVIDIA nvenc**: Hardware video encoder\n- **X11 Display Capture**: Screen capture method for streaming\n- **Moonlight**: Client application for connecting to Sunshine\n- **Steam Big Picture**: TV-friendly Steam interface\n- **systemd**: Service management (though Sunshine runs standalone)\n\n## 3. Files and Code Sections\n\n### `/home/lsm/Nextcloud/k3s-cluster/steam/host-streaming-setup.md`\n- Source document containing all 6 phases of the setup\n- Read to understand the implementation steps\n\n### `/usr/local/bin/start-streaming`\n- Script to start the streaming session\n- Final version:\n```bash\n#!/bin/bash\n# Start streaming session on lsnode-3\n\nUSER=${SUDO_USER:-lsm}\nDISPLAY=:0\nXAUTH=/var/run/lightdm/root/:0\n\necho \"Starting streaming session for user: $USER...\"\n\n# Start LightDM if not running\nif ! systemctl is-active --quiet lightdm; then\n    echo \"Starting LightDM...\"\n    sudo systemctl start lightdm\n    sleep 5\nfi\n\n# Wait for display to be ready\necho \"Waiting for display to be ready...\"\nfor i in {1..30}; do\n    if xset -display $DISPLAY q >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n        echo \"Display is ready.\"\n        break\n    fi\n    sleep 1\ndone\n\n# Check if Sunshine is already running\nif pgrep -x sunshine >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    echo \"Sunshine is already running.\"\nelse\n    echo \"Starting Sunshine...\"\n    # Run Sunshine as the lightdm user with proper X access\n    sudo -u lightdm DISPLAY=$DISPLAY XAUTHORITY=$XAUTH sunshine /etc/sunshine/sunshine.conf &\n    sleep 3\nfi\n\n# Start Steam in Big Picture mode\nif ! pgrep -x steam >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    echo \"Starting Steam in Big Picture mode...\"\n    sudo -u lightdm DISPLAY=$DISPLAY XAUTHORITY=$XAUTH steam -silent -bigpicture &\nelse\n    echo \"Steam is already running.\"\nfi\n\necho \"\"\necho \"Streaming session started.\"\necho \"Connect via Moonlight to: $(hostname -I | awk '{print $1}')\"\necho \"Sunshine web interface: https://$(hostname -I | awk '{print $1}'):47990\"\n```\n\n### `/usr/local/bin/stop-streaming`\n```bash\n#!/bin/bash\n# Stop streaming session on lsnode-3\n\necho \"Stopping streaming session...\"\n\n# Stop Steam\nif pgrep -x steam >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    echo \"Stopping Steam...\"\n    pkill steam\n    sleep 2\nfi\n\n# Stop Sunshine\nif pgrep -x sunshine >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    echo \"Stopping Sunshine...\"\n    pkill sunshine\n    sleep 1\nfi\n\necho \"\"\necho \"Streaming session stopped.\"\necho \"LightDM is still running. Use 'sudo systemctl stop lightdm' to stop the display.\"\n```\n\n### `/etc/sunshine/sunshine.conf`\n```\nlog_level = info\nweb_enabled = true\nport = 47989\nhttps_port = 47990\ngame_port = 47991\nwidth = 1920\nheight = 1080\nfps = 60\nbitrate = 20000\nencoder = nvenc\nhwaccel = true\ninput_source = auto\nmulticast = false\nrecovery_level = 150\naudio_device = default\naudio_bitrate = 256\nautostart = false\n```\n\n### `/home/lsm/.config/autostart/steam-bigpicture.desktop`\n```\n[Desktop Entry]\nVersion=1.0\nType=Application\nName=Steam Big Picture\nExec=steam -silent -bigpicture\nHidden=false\nNoDisplay=false\nX-GNOME-Autostart-enabled=true\nComment=Start Steam in Big Picture mode for gaming\n```\n\n## 4. Errors and Fixes\n\n### Error 1: Sunshine PPA not found\n- **Issue**: `sudo add-apt-repository ppa:briando/sunshine` failed with \"ppa not found\"\n- **Fix**: Downloaded Sunshine directly from GitHub releases (v2025.924.154138) as `sunshine-ubuntu-24.04-amd64.deb`\n\n### Error 2: Steam installer missing i386 dependencies\n- **Issue**: `steam-installer` depends on `steam-libs-i386` which wasn't available\n- **Fix**: Added i386 architecture with `dpkg --add-architecture i386` and ran `apt update`\n\n### Error 3: Sunshine config flag format wrong\n- **Issue**: Using `--config /path/to/config` caused \"Unknown command: config\" error\n- **Fix**: Changed to positional argument: `sunshine /path/to/config.conf`\n\n### Error 4: Sunshine can't access X display\n- **Issue**: \"Authorization required, but no authorization protocol specified\" - Sunshine couldn't access the X11 display\n- **Attempted Fix**: Tried running as lightdm user with `XAUTHORITY=/var/run/lightdm/root/:0`\n- **Root Cause**: LightDM is running a login screen, not a user session. Sunshine needs an active user session to capture.\n\n### Error 5: All encoders failing (nvenc, vaapi, software)\n- **Issue**: \"Fatal: Unable to find display or encoder during startup\"\n- **Root Cause**: Without a valid display capture source, encoders cannot initialize. The X11 capture method fails because there's no logged-in user session.\n\n### Error 6: Port conflicts when restarting Sunshine\n- **Issue**: \"Couldn't bind RTSP server to port [48010], Address already in use\"\n- **Fix**: Used `sudo pkill -9 sunshine` to force kill all instances\n\n### User Feedback on Rebooting\n- **User Warning**: \"you really shouldn't reboot because you are running on that node\"\n- **Impact**: Avoided reboot after NVIDIA driver installation; drivers loaded without reboot\n\n## 5. The goal is to transform lsnode-3 (a K8s node with 3 NVIDIA GPUs) into a streaming gaming server that can:\n- Stream games via Sunshine/Moonlight\n- Run Steam in Big Picture mode\n- Maintain K8s GPU access for existing workloads (llmmll)\n- Operate on-demand without auto-starting on boot\n\n## 2. Key Technical Concepts\n\n- **Kubernetes GPU Operator**: Manages NVIDIA drivers and GPU access in K8s\n- **ClusterPolicy**: NVIDIA GPU Operator configuration resource\n- **Sunshine**: Self-hosted game stream server for Moonlight clients\n- **LightDM**: Lightweight display manager for X11\n- **KDE Plasma Desktop**: Desktop environment for the streaming session\n- **NVIDIA nvenc**: Hardware video encoder\n- **X11 Display Capture**: Screen capture method for streaming\n- **Moonlight**: Client application for connecting to Sunshine\n- **Steam Big Picture**: TV-friendly Steam interface\n- **systemd**: Service management (though Sunshine runs standalone)\n\n## 3. Files and Code Sections\n\n### `/home/lsm/Nextcloud/k3s-cluster/steam/host-streaming-setup.md`\n- Source document containing all 6 phases of the setup\n- Read to understand the implementation steps\n\n### `/usr/local/bin/start-streaming`\n- Script to start the streaming session\n- Final version:\n```bash\n#!/bin/bash\n# Start streaming session on lsnode-3\n\nUSER=${SUDO_USER:-lsm}\nDISPLAY=:0\nXAUTH=/var/run/lightdm/root/:0\n\necho \"Starting streaming session for user: $USER...\"\n\n# Start LightDM if not running\nif ! systemctl is-active --quiet lightdm; then\n    echo \"Starting LightDM...\"\n    sudo systemctl start lightdm\n    sleep 5\nfi\n\n# Wait for display to be ready\necho \"Waiting for display to be ready...\"\nfor i in {1..30}; do\n    if xset -display $DISPLAY q >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n        echo \"Display is ready.\"\n        break\n    fi\n    sleep 1\ndone\n\n# Check if Sunshine is already running\nif pgrep -x sunshine >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    echo \"Sunshine is already running.\"\nelse\n    echo \"Starting Sunshine...\"\n    # Run Sunshine as the lightdm user with proper X access\n    sudo -u lightdm DISPLAY=$DISPLAY XAUTHORITY=$XAUTH sunshine /etc/sunshine/sunshine.conf &\n    sleep 3\nfi\n\n# Start Steam in Big Picture mode\nif ! pgrep -x steam >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    echo \"Starting Steam in Big Picture mode...\"\n    sudo -u lightdm DISPLAY=$DISPLAY XAUTHORITY=$XAUTH steam -silent -bigpicture &\nelse\n    echo \"Steam is already running.\"\nfi\n\necho \"\"\necho \"Streaming session started.\"\necho \"Connect via Moonlight to: $(hostname -I | awk '{print $1}')\"\necho \"Sunshine web interface: https://$(hostname -I | awk '{print $1}'):47990\"\n```\n\n### `/usr/local/bin/stop-streaming`\n```bash\n#!/bin/bash\n# Stop streaming session on lsnode-3\n\necho \"Stopping streaming session...\"\n\n# Stop Steam\nif pgrep -x steam >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    echo \"Stopping Steam...\"\n    pkill steam\n    sleep 2\nfi\n\n# Stop Sunshine\nif pgrep -x sunshine >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    echo \"Stopping Sunshine...\"\n    pkill sunshine\n    sleep 1\nfi\n\necho \"\"\necho \"Streaming session stopped.\"\necho \"LightDM is still running. Use 'sudo systemctl stop lightdm' to stop the display.\"\n```\n\n### `/etc/sunshine/sunshine.conf`\n```\nlog_level = info\nweb_enabled = true\nport = 47989\nhttps_port = 47990\ngame_port = 47991\nwidth = 1920\nheight = 1080\nfps = 60\nbitrate = 20000\nencoder = nvenc\nhwaccel = true\ninput_source = auto\nmulticast = false\nrecovery_level = 150\naudio_device = default\naudio_bitrate = 256\nautostart = false\n```\n\n### `/home/lsm/.config/autostart/steam-bigpicture.desktop`\n```\n[Desktop Entry]\nVersion=1.0\nType=Application\nName=Steam Big Picture\nExec=steam -silent -bigpicture\nHidden=false\nNoDisplay=false\nX-GNOME-Autostart-enabled=true\nComment=Start Steam in Big Picture mode for gaming\n```\n\n## 4. Errors and Fixes\n\n### Error 1: Sunshine PPA not found\n- **Issue**: `sudo add-apt-repository ppa:briando/sunshine` failed with \"ppa not found\"\n- **Fix**: Downloaded Sunshine directly from GitHub releases (v2025.924.154138) as `sunshine-ubuntu-24.04-amd64.deb`\n\n### Error 2: Steam installer missing i386 dependencies\n- **Issue**: `steam-installer` depends on `steam-libs-i386` which wasn't available\n- **Fix**: Added i386 architecture with `dpkg --add-architecture i386` and ran `apt update`\n\n### Error 3: Sunshine config flag format wrong\n- **Issue**: Using `--config /path/to/config` caused \"Unknown command: config\" error\n- **Fix**: Changed to positional argument: `sunshine /path/to/config.conf`\n\n### Error 4: Sunshine can't access X display\n- **Issue**: \"Authorization required, but no authorization protocol specified\" - Sunshine couldn't access the X11 display\n- **Attempted Fix**: Tried running as lightdm user with `XAUTHORITY=/var/run/lightdm/root/:0`\n- **Root Cause**: LightDM is running a login screen, not a user session. Sunshine needs an active user session to capture.\n\n### Error 5: All encoders failing (nvenc, vaapi, software)\n- **Issue**: \"Fatal: Unable to find display or encoder during startup\"\n- **Root Cause**: Without a valid display capture source, encoders cannot initialize. The X11 capture method fails because there's no logged-in user session.\n\n### Error 6: Port conflicts when restarting Sunshine\n- **Issue**: \"Couldn't bind RTSP server to port [48010], Address already in use\"\n- **Fix**: Used `sudo pkill -9 sunshine` to force kill all instances\n\n### User Feedback on Rebooting\n- **User Warning**: \"you really shouldn't reboot because you are running on that node\"\n- **Impact**: Avoided reboot after NVIDIA driver installation; drivers loaded without reboot\n\n## 5. Problem Solving\n\n### Solved Problems:\n1. **Package installation**: Successfully installed KDE Plasma, LightDM, NVIDIA drivers, Sunshine, and Steam\n2. **K8s GPU Operator reconfiguration**: Disabled driver management in ClusterPolicy without downtime\n3. **GPU access verification**: Confirmed containers can still access GPUs via device-plugin\n4. **Script creation**: Created start/stop streaming scripts\n\n### Ongoing Troubleshooting:\n**Core Issue**: Sunshine cannot capture the display because:\n- LightDM is running a login greeter (unity-greeter), not a user desktop session\n- Sunshine needs an active X11 session with a logged-in user to capture screens\n- The nvenc encoder fails because it depends on having a valid display source\n\n**Potential Solutions**:\n1. Configure a user to auto-login to the desktop session\n2. Use a dummy display driver with virtual framebuffer\n3. Configure Sunshine to use a different capture method (X11 screenshot)\n4. Key Technical Concepts\n\n- **Kubernetes GPU Operator**: Manages NVIDIA drivers and GPU access in K8s\n- **ClusterPolicy**: NVIDIA GPU Operator configuration resource\n- **Sunshine**: Self-hosted game stream server for Moonlight clients\n- **LightDM**: Lightweight display manager for X11\n- **KDE Plasma Desktop**: Desktop environment for the streaming session\n- **NVIDIA nvenc**: Hardware video encoder\n- **X11 Display Capture**: Screen capture method for streaming\n- **Moonlight**: Client application for connecting to Sunshine\n- **Steam Big Picture**: TV-friendly Steam interface\n- **systemd**: Service management (though Sunshine runs standalone)\n\n## 3. pgrep -x steam >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    echo \"Starting Steam in Big Picture mode...\"\n    sudo -u lightdm DISPLAY=$DISPLAY XAUTHORITY=$XAUTH steam -silent -bigpicture &\nelse\n    echo \"Steam is already running.\"\nfi\n\necho \"\"\necho \"Streaming session started.\"\necho \"Connect via Moonlight to: $(hostname -I | awk '{print $1}')\"\necho \"Sunshine web interface: https://$(hostname -I | awk '{print $1}'):47990\"\n```\n\n### `/usr/local/bin/stop-streaming`\n```bash\n#!/bin/bash\n# Stop streaming session on lsnode-3\n\necho \"Stopping streaming session...\"\n\n# Stop Steam\nif pgrep -x steam >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    echo \"Stopping Steam...\"\n    pkill steam\n    sleep 2\nfi\n\n# Stop Sunshine\nif pgrep -x sunshine >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    echo \"Stopping Sunshine...\"\n    pkill sunshine\n    sleep 1\nfi\n\necho \"\"\necho \"Streaming session stopped.\"\necho \"LightDM is still running.
